analysis.title: The Fed delivers a hawkish hold
key_insights: The Fed held the target policy rate at 3.75% to 4.00% in a 10-2 vote on 28 October 2026, after its September hike. Two members dissented in favor of another increase.

The statement was brief, offered no forward guidance, and cited tighter financial conditions and incoming information as the basis for waiting. Nuveen reads this as signaling another hike by year-end, likely in December, followed by a prolonged pause.
Chair Warsh was constructive, saying the 'overwhelming judgement at the FOMC is that monetary medicine is starting to work.' He said more work is needed on price stability.
The Fed will hold one strategy-focused meeting in 2027 with no vote or statement, and two in 2028. Eight meetings per year were judged the 'right number.'

Core inflation has surprised to the upside. Last year's government shutdown distorts year-over-year comparisons and is likely to lift them in coming months. Nuveen still expects inflation to moderate through 2027.
Crude rose from $101 to $115 since the last Fed meeting amid escalating U.S./Iran tensions, and diesel is near $6.30/gallon. Nuveen says energy could decide whether a hike comes this year.
Nuveen forecasts core PCE at 3.0% by year-end 2026 and 2.5% in 2027. It forecasts the 10-year Treasury yield at 4.95% by year-end and 4.75% by end-2027.
Nuveen says the data does not justify the additional hikes markets are pricing through year-end 2027. It sees the fed funds rate near neutral and risks skewed toward a prolonged pause.
September payrolls rose 29,000 after a revised 133,000 in August. Unemployment was 4.2%, and wage growth was 0.1% m/m and 3.0% y/y. Nuveen reads this as stabilization.

Nuveen sees room to add credit selectively. It favors securitized credit (CMBS, ABS, CLOs), preferred securities, listed infrastructure, and a convertible arbitrage, long-short credit and opportunistic CLO framework.
It is cautious on extending duration and favors shorter-to-medium maturities. Investment grade spreads near 90 bps have been tighter only 4% of the time over 25 years.

sector_views.rationale: Yields exceed investment grade corporates with shorter duration and lower rate sensitivity. CLOs have near-zero duration of about 0.25 years and historically lower default rates than corporate bonds.
Spreads have tightened and outperformed most US investment grade sectors this year. About 80% of issuers are banks, insurers and utilities, and AT1 supply is about 80% issued.
AI-driven power demand outpaces transmission and generation build-out, which supports scarcity value for utilities. Correlation with technology has turned negative.
Fiscal concerns, heavy AI-related issuance and energy risks may keep upward pressure on yields. Nuveen favors shorter-to-medium maturities.

earnings_insights: The S&P 500 forward P/E sits above its long-run average. Analysts forecast double-digit EPS growth, more than triple the 7.5% long-run average.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The Fed held after its September hike on a 10-2 vote, with both dissents favoring a hike.
Two dissents for a hike reflect uncertainty over the inflation outlook, in contrast with September's unanimous hike.
Slowed from a revised 133,000 in August but above the 45,000 average pace of the past year. Nuveen reads it as stabilization.
Slowing wage growth supports the Fed's 2% inflation goal.
Described as consistent with the Fed's 2% target.
Led markets to price in a renewed hiking cycle, though Nuveen sees limited evidence of a reflating economy.

September Fed projection reflecting a temporary inflation shock.
September Fed projection showing solid growth.
The Fed projects the shock fading.

Nuveen's forecast, with fiscal concerns and AI-related issuance adding upward pressure.

trade_ideas.rationale: Higher yield than investment grade corporates with shorter duration and lower rate sensitivity.
Spreads have tightened, issuers are fundamentally strong, and technicals support the asset class.

trade_ideas.rationale: AI power demand creates scarcity value for utilities, and correlation with technology has turned negative.

trade_ideas.description: Multi-strategy credit framework: convertible arbitrage, long-short credit and opportunistic CLO debt and equity
trade_ideas.rationale: The three strategies aim to perform across market environments and diversify against equities and traditional credit.
trade_ideas.risk: Convertible arbitrage carries leverage, liquidity and credit risks.

trade_ideas.description: Stay cautious on duration and favor shorter-to-medium maturities
trade_ideas.rationale: Energy risks, fiscal concerns and heavy AI-related issuance may push yields up.
trade_ideas.risk: A negative growth shock would favor extending duration.

risk_factors: Oil price escalation tied to U.S./Iran tensions could force another hike.
Core inflation upside surprises and shutdown-related distortions in year-over-year comparisons.
Tariff pass-through, tech spending and fiscal policy are swing factors.
Heavy AI-related issuance and fiscal concerns could push yields higher.
Stretched valuations in equities and credit, including investment grade spreads near 90 bps.
Recent equity market volatility could weigh on growth.
vol_and_positioning: Recent equity market volatility is a potential headwind to third quarter growth.
The 10-year Treasury yield rose only about 5 bps since the September meeting, which masks sharp intra-period swings.
Convertible bonds' embedded optionality can benefit from volatility. The global convertible market is $600 billion with record liquidity.
geopolitical: Escalating U.S./Iran tensions have pushed oil and gas prices sharply higher.
Renewed geopolitical tensions complicate the inflation picture.
Tariffs, and their pass-through to prices, remain a swing factor for inflation.

tension_points.bull_case: Hot core CPI and firm PPI led markets to price a renewed hiking cycle. Two FOMC members dissented for a hike, citing inflation risks from repeated supply shocks, and oil at $115 could force a year-end hike.
tension_points.bear_case: Nuveen sees limited evidence of a reflating economy. It expects one more hike by year-end and then a prolonged pause, with inflation moderating through 2027 as tariff pass-through fades and shelter costs cool.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Escalating U.S./Iran tensions pushing oil and gas prices higher could decide whether another hike comes this year.
